latin.292:
§. VI.
Hactenus de Limitibus Consociationis Ecclesiasticae, Materialiter consideratis, diximus. Formaliter considerati, seu quatenus limitationis hujus actum designant, duobus quasi gradibus conspicui fiunt,
latin.293: quorum alter ad Tolerantiam duntaxat procedit, Consociatio partialis dicendus;
latin.294: alter ad perfectam Unionem exporrigitur, totalemque consociationem Ecclesiasticam conficit.
latin.295: Dico duobus gradibus conspicuos fieri Consociationis Ecclesiasticae limites, scilicet ex vulgi opinione, quâ Tolerantia Politica cum Tolerantia Ecclesiastica confunditur;
latin.296: alioquin, qui tolerandus Ecclesiasticè est, ei cum Fundamento Fidei & Fundamentalibus Christianae Religionis convenire necesse est:
latin.297: Cui autem convenit cum Fundamentalibus, hic idem eô ipsô, quòd tolerandus, eâdem quoque Ecclesiastica Consociatione copulandus copulatusque est.

pass_a.292: §. VI. Thus far we have spoken of the Limits of Ecclesiastical Consociation considered Materially. Considered Formally — that is, insofar as they designate the act of this limitation — they become conspicuous in two grades, as it were,
pass_a.293: of which the one proceeds only as far as Tolerance, and is to be called partial Consociation;
pass_a.294: the other is stretched out to perfect Union, and completes total Ecclesiastical Consociation.
pass_a.295: I say that the limits of Ecclesiastical Consociation become conspicuous in two grades, namely from the opinion of the vulgar, by which Political Tolerance is confused with Ecclesiastical Tolerance;
pass_a.296: otherwise, whoever is to be tolerated ecclesiastically must necessarily agree with the Foundation of the Faith and the Fundamentals of the Christian Religion:
pass_a.297: But to whom there is agreement with the Fundamentals, this same one, by that very fact that he is to be tolerated, is also to be coupled and has been coupled in the same Ecclesiastical Consociation.

292: §. VI. So far we have treated the limits of church Consociation on the material side.
Taken formally — as naming the act of drawing that limit — they show up in roughly two degrees.
293: One degree reaches only as far as Tolerance.
That grade is rightly called partial Consociation.
294: The other stretches out to perfect Union.
There it completes total ecclesiastical Consociation.
295: I mark those two grades chiefly because common opinion mixes Political Tolerance with Ecclesiastical Tolerance.
That confusion is what makes the double ladder look sharp to the crowd.
296: Otherwise, anyone to be tolerated in the church must already agree with the Foundation of the Faith and the Fundamentals of the Christian religion.
Without that agreement, ecclesiastical tolerance does not even begin.
297: But whoever does agree with the Fundamentals is, by that very fact that he is tolerable, also to be joined — and already joined — in the same church Consociation.
Stop before Annotatio VI (Classes of controversies among Evangelicals).
